ai.description: This slender snake reaches 70–90 cm. It is brownish-grey with distinct, white-edged dark crossbands and a characteristic V-shaped mark on the nape. It possesses enlarged, blade-like rear teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Oligodon albocinctus* is the presence of distinct, thin white cross-bands edged in black, which contrast sharply against a reddish-brown body.
ai.habitat: The White-barred Kukri Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found in hilly regions ranging from lowlands up to approximately 2,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The White-barred Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice open reptile eggs for consumption.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon albocinctus* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–7 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, roughly from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon albocinctus* is found in Northeast India, primarily across the Eastern Himalayas and Assam, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 2,000 meters in elevation.
